profiles.meeting_scenario: A brainstorming meeting in an ML research lab where a PI and a senior PhD student are developing a follow-up project inspired by a paper that designs CNN architectures from recursion formulas rather than ad hoc block motifs. The lab has a six-week window for a workshop submission, and they want 2-3 candidate directions that extend the formula-centric view beyond the original ResNet-based case study while still being practical to prototype. The agenda is to explore what kinds of recurrence-based design ideas would feel publishably novel, how broadly the mathematical framing should reach, and what the smallest convincing experimental package would be for selecting one direction. The expected outcome is a shortlist of candidate ideas plus an apparent shared plan for what 'generalized formula,' 'new family,' 'minimal validation,' and 'baseline ResNet setup' will mean for the next week of work.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Neural architecture design, optimization theory, and empirical deep learning
members.background: Maya leads a university ML lab that publishes at the intersection of theory-motivated model design and practical vision benchmarks, and she has recently been favoring papers that offer a clean conceptual lens with a manageable experimental package.
members.private_state: She wants a workshop-ready direction that sounds genuinely new in its mathematical framing but can be executed quickly by reusing the lab's existing ResNet codepath and avoiding a broad implementation or benchmarking expansion before the deadline.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a direction is 'novel,' the decisive novelty can come from a new recursion-derived interpretation or update equation even if the instantiated network still looks structurally ResNet-like.
A 'new architecture family' can still be a family of residual-style networks as long as the generating formula systematically changes the block dynamics and yields a coherent conceptual story.

To 'generalize the formula' in a six-week workshop project means enlarging the mathematical template around residual recursions, not necessarily covering dense reuse or fundamentally different connectivity graphs.

Given the deadline, 'minimal validation' means the bare minimum needed to make a credible workshop claim: a clean CIFAR study and at most one stronger confirmation run using standard lab infrastructure.
Inside the lab, 'baseline ResNet setup' naturally refers to their in-house reproduction recipe and codebase unless someone explicitly says they are reproducing the original paper settings.

members.name: Arjun Patel
members.expertise: Architecture benchmarking, reproducibility, and large-scale vision experiments
members.background: Arjun is a senior PhD student who has spent several years re-implementing classic and modern CNN families, and he habitually evaluates ideas by whether they remain convincing under cross-family comparisons and reviewer-style scrutiny.
members.private_state: He wants the brainstorming to land on a direction that could later scale into a main-conference paper, so he is quietly steering toward ideas that are structurally broad, benchmark-defensible, and not vulnerable to accusations that the gains only come from one tuned recipe.
hidden_assumptions: When researchers call an architecture direction 'novel,' that usually has to involve structural novelty in connectivity or applicability across materially different architecture families, not just a cleaner mathematical description of a ResNet variant.

A 'new architecture family' should plausibly extend beyond residual-style backbones; otherwise reviewers will treat it as another local ResNet modification rather than a real family-level contribution.
To 'generalize the formula' means producing a recurrence language broad enough to express multiple existing skip/reuse patterns—ideally residual, dense, and multi-branch cases—under one framework.

With only six weeks, 'minimal validation' still means the minimum needed to avoid a predictable rejection for weak evidence: at least some cross-family transfer or replication showing the recurrence idea survives beyond one lucky setting.

When someone mentions the 'baseline ResNet setup,' the sensible default is the canonical public or literature-aligned baseline used in prior architecture comparisons, not a convenience-tuned internal recipe.

misalignment_points.topic: What makes a 'new architecture family' novel
misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly discuss finding a 'new architecture family' that would feel genuinely 'novel' from the recursion-formula perspective.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 hears 'novel' and 'new family' as conceptual novelty: a recurrence-derived residual-style family counts if the governing formula is new and principled, even when the visible connectivity remains close to standard ResNet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 hears 'novel' and 'new family' as structural novelty: it should induce or at least cover meaningfully different connectivity behavior across more than the residual lineage, otherwise it is not really a new family.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In brainstorming, 'novel' and 'family' are flattering, high-level terms that both expect the other to interpret sensibly; because they are screening ideas rather than writing claims yet, the conceptual-vs-structural distinction stays comfortably implicit.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the strongest direction may be to 'generalize the recursion formula.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means broadening the residual-update template—such as adding higher-order state terms, gated carryover, or cross-stage recurrence—while staying within architectures that are straightforward extensions of ResNet-like stagewise networks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means a unifying formalism broad enough to recover several existing connectivity regimes, including residual, dense, and perhaps aggregated multi-branch reuse, under one recurrence notation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds naturally ambitious and positive, and both versions are mathematically plausible continuations of the seed paper, so neither participant feels a need to pin down the boundary during an exploratory discussion.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'minimal validation' under the six-week deadline
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree they only need 'minimal validation' to decide on a workshop-scale direction within six weeks.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes 'minimal validation' to mean the bare minimum to get a workshop paper over the line on schedule: for example, CIFAR-100 on ResNet-32/110 plus one confirmatory ImageNet-100 or ResNet-50 run using the lab's standard recipe.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes 'minimal validation' to mean the bare minimum to avoid an obvious rigor objection even at workshop level: for example, evidence that the idea is not confined to one residual backbone, plus enough repeatability or ablation to show the gain is not just recipe noise.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same deadline-aware phrase and both are sincerely talking about the 'minimum,' but one anchors it to submission feasibility while the other anchors it to rejection-risk; because no exact experiment table is assigned yet, the difference remains latent.

misalignment_points.topic: Which concrete 'baseline ResNet setup' is being held fixed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They say comparisons should use the 'baseline ResNet setup' and keep the recipe fixed.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the lab's internal ResNet training stack—e.g., their current ResNet-50/ResNet-110 code with cosine decay, label smoothing, mixup off, and the augmentation defaults from the lab's last reproduction cycle.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the canonical public baseline aligned with architecture papers they would cite—e.g., the published or publicly reproducible ResNet settings used in standard CIFAR/ImageNet comparisons rather than the lab's convenience baseline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Inside ML groups, 'the ResNet baseline' is common shorthand that usually feels self-explanatory, and both think they are invoking the obvious standard reference implementation, so the specific anchor never gets verbalized.

turns.inner_thought: We need a workshop-ready idea, not a sprawling architecture program. If we can derive a principled new update rule that still instantiates as a residual-style network in our existing code, that already qualifies as a new architecture family to me. And minimal validation should stay tight enough to finish on time: a clean CIFAR study and maybe one stronger confirmation run, nothing more.
turns.utterance: Okay, we really have about six weeks to turn the recursion-formula paper into a workshop-worthy follow-up. I'd like us to leave today with two or three candidate directions that could honestly read as a new architecture family, but without committing ourselves to a long build-out. What feels genuinely novel here, and what can we support with only minimal validation?

turns.inner_thought: A higher-order residual recurrence is exactly the sweet spot: mathematically fresh, easy to motivate, and cheap to implement by reusing the lab's ResNet path. That's enough novelty if the recursion framing is clean.
turns.utterance: One concrete option is a parameterized recurrence with a little more state in it—some carryover, maybe a gated update. That would let us generalize the formula in a clean way while still keeping the implementation path very manageable.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep this from ballooning. Broad framing is fine, but we should not let it force a bunch of extra prototypes before we even know which direction we want. Minimal validation here means enough evidence to pick the workshop candidate, not a full review-proof package.
turns.utterance: Right. I just want us to stay disciplined on scope, because in this six-week window we only need minimal validation before we commit to one direction. I don't want the framing to quietly force a huge implementation matrix up front.

turns.inner_thought: I agree on staying lean, but 'minimal' still has to clear the obvious criticism threshold. If it's only one lucky residual setting, people will dismiss it immediately. I should signal robustness without spelling out the breadth I want.
turns.utterance: Totally, minimal validation is the right target. I just think the minimum should still make it hard for someone to dismiss the result as a one-off artifact. Even at workshop scale, that basic robustness matters.

turns.inner_thought: We should keep our in-house ResNet training stack fixed and only touch the recurrence. That lets us move quickly and avoid detours into recipe tuning. When I say the baseline ResNet setup, I mean our lab's code and defaults.
turns.utterance: Agreed. On the experimental side, I think comparisons should use the baseline ResNet setup and keep the recipe fixed. Then if we see movement, we can attribute it to the recursion rather than training changes.

turns.inner_thought: Yes—anchor to the canonical literature-aligned ResNet baseline so the numbers are legible against prior papers. I assume that's what she means by the baseline setup.
turns.utterance: I agree. If we stay faithful to the standard ResNet baseline, it'll also be much easier to position the results against prior architecture papers. It keeps the narrative cleaner.

turns.inner_thought: Let me keep the options close to things we can actually ship: higher-order residual recursion, stage-level memory, or a recurrence-derived block generator. Any of these could count as a new architecture family if the math tells a coherent story, even if the instantiated network stays pretty ResNet-like.

Any of those could plausibly count as a new architecture family if the mathematical framing is clean enough.

turns.inner_thought: My filter is still breadth: which candidate gives a recurrence language that spans the widest range of configurations and won't look narrow later. I need to phrase that vaguely enough that Maya hears it as healthy ambition, not a demand for cross-family scope right now.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. turns.inner_thought: I still want the higher-order residual option. It's fastest in our current codebase, gives the cleanest conceptual lens, and fits what I consider minimal validation under our existing ResNet recipe.
turns.utterance: Given the timeline, I'm still leaning toward the higher-order residual idea as the lead candidate. It seems fastest to stand up in our codebase, and it still fits a minimal validation package before the workshop deadline if we keep everything under our baseline setup.
